chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Washa', from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abu Maryam, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'What do you say regarding the urines of the animals and their droppings?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'As for their urines, wash if it hits you, and as for their droppings, it is more than that.'
ai.seo_question: What is the difference in ritual purification between animal urine and animal droppings in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: In this concise narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between the ritual impurity (najāsah) of animal urine, which necessitates simple washing (ghasl), and their droppings, which require a more rigorous purification process. This distinction reflects the broader Shia jurisprudential principle that different animal excretions carry varying degrees of impurity, influencing the method of tathir (purification) for prayer garments. The brevity of the text underscores the practical application of these rules in daily life, emphasizing the necessity of distinguishing between minor and major impurities.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Washa, from Aban Bin usman, from Abu Maryam who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘What are you<sup>asws</sup> saying regarding the urines of the animal and their droppings?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘As for their urines, so wash if it hits you, and as for their droppings, so it is more than that’.
en.sarwar: 5. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu‘alla’ ibn Muhammad from al-Washsha’ from Aban ibn ‘Uthman from abu Maryam who has said the following: “I once said to abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘What do you say about the urine of animals and their dung?’
He (the Imam) said, ‘Because of their urine you must wash and their dung is more than that.’”
